Definition: from G1537 and G2233; to consider out (aloud), i.e. rehearse, unfold:--declare, tell.
BiblicalUsage: exēgéomai means declare, tell. In John 1:18, the text says "he hath declared [him]." In Acts 10:8, the text says "And when he had declared all [these] things unto them."
TheologicalSignificance: Reading exēgéomai this way, I believe God's Word means what it says, and this word is part of how He speaks plainly to us. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: The Resurrection; Jerusalem Council; Peter and Cornelius
